The river is dying. Satellite images confirm what locals have known for a decade. Water levels have dropped forty percent since 2010. The fish are disappearing. The birds that fed on the fish are gone too. Farmers upstream divert more water every year to irrigate crops that were never meant to grow in a desert. Cities downstream ration what is left. Lawns are banned. Car washes are closed. Restaurants serve water only on request. The legal fights over allocation have been grinding through courts for years. Everyone has a claim. Nobody has a solution. Engineers propose desalination plants. Environmentalists push for reduced consumption. Politicians promise compromise and deliver gridlock. The river does not care about politics. It responds to physics. Less inflow means less water. Less water means collapse -- ecological, economic, and social. The clock is running. The river does not negotiate. It just shrinks.
